spec.description: The function receives a context with time-of-day flags, player pixel coordinates, world data (tile grid, dimensions, and an optional spawn elevation), an existing enemies array, and an optional spawn cap. It uses a fallback cap if `spawnCap` is falsy and returns early if the current enemy count already meets or exceeds that limit. Player depth is derived by converting the pixel position to tiles and subtracting a world-level spawn reference, defaulting if absent. A base spawn probability is selected based on daytime, nighttime, or blood moon, then multiplied by cumulative factors as the depth crosses successive thresholds. An independent random check is performed; if it fails, no enemy is produced. Otherwise, a candidate spawn tile is computed by picking a random angle uniformly, a random distance from a bounded interval, scaling the vertical offset by a constant factor, rounding to integer tile coordinates, and discarding if the result lies within a narrow border margin of the world edges. The tile at the candidate position must be inactive (air) and the tile directly below must be active (ground), or the attempt is abandoned. Enemy type is chosen via random threshold comparisons: during nighttime certain types are weighted, some with a minimum depth requirement; during daytime deeper depths unlock additional types; a blood moon overrides all prior selections with a more dangerous type set. The resulting type is resolved from a globally defined table. A new enemy object is then constructed with an id combining a timestamp and random number, a position centered on the tile, zero velocities, stats from the definition, and an AI state containing a random phase and zero jump delays. This enemy is pushed onto the input `enemies` array, mutating it, and the function returns an object containing that same array reference.
